question: Who is the author of the book 'An Equal Music'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram Seth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vikram Seth** is the acclaimed author of the novel **'An Equal Music'**, which was published in the year **1999**.
 
• The book is a **romantic novel** that revolves around the lives of professional musicians, specifically a violinist named **Michael Holme** and a pianist named **Julia McNicholl**.
 
• The narrative is deeply infused with **classical music** themes, featuring works by composers such as **Beethoven**, **Vivaldi**, and **Bach**, reflecting **Vikram Seth's** own passion for music. ***Hence, the option containing Vikram Seth is correct.***
 
• The story is set primarily in **London**, with significant portions taking place in **Vienna** and **Venice**, capturing the atmosphere of European musical culture.
 
• **'An Equal Music'** is noted for its lyrical prose and its exploration of themes like **lost love**, the **nature of memory**, and the **physicality of sound**, particularly Michael’s struggle with Julia’s deafness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kiran Desai:**

 
 
• She is an **Indian author** who won the **Man Booker Prize** in **2006** for her novel **'The Inheritance of Loss'**.
 
• Her first novel, **'Hullabaloo in the Guava Orchard'**, was published in **1998** and won the **Betty Trask Award**.
 
• She is the daughter of the famous novelist **Anita Desai**.
 
 
 
• **Zulfikar Ghose:**
 
 
• He was a **Pakistani-American** novelist, poet, and essayist born in **Sialkot** in **1935**.
 
• He is well-known for his trilogy **'The Incredible Brazilian'** and the novel **'The Murder of Aziz Khan'** (**1967**).
 
• His work often explores the **post-colonial identity** and the history of South Asia.
 
 
 
• **Shiva Naipaul:**
 
 
• He was a **Trinidadian-British** novelist and journalist, and the younger brother of the Nobel laureate **V.S. Naipaul**.
 
• His notable works include **'Fireflies'** (**1970**), which won the **John Llewellyn Rhys Prize**, and **'The Chip-Chip Gatherers'** (**1973**).
 
• He was known for his sharp **satirical style** and observations on the **Caribbean diaspora**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vikram Seth** was born in **Kolkata**, India, in **1952** and is widely regarded as one of India's most versatile writers.
 
• His most famous work, **'A Suitable Boy'**, published in **1993**, is one of the **longest novels** ever published in a single volume in the **English language**.
 
• He has received numerous awards, including the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1988** for **'The Golden Gate'** and the **Padma Shri** in **2007** for his contributions to Literature and Education.
 
• **'The Golden Gate'** (**1986**) is a unique **novel in verse**, written entirely in **Onegin stanzas**, showcasing his mastery over diverse literary forms.
 
• Apart from fiction, he is a prolific **poet** and has published works like **'Mappings'** and **'Beastly Tales from Here and There'**.
